Cautiously positive, nudged higher. The FOMC’s June 16, 2021 statement notes strengthening activity and employment under very accommodative policy. Beige Book insights across districts reinforce this tone: economic activity picked up with consumer and business spending contributing, labor markets tightened amid ongoing labor availability concerns that are pushing up wage pressures, and prices moved higher. Residential real estate remained strong while commercial real estate was more uneven, and overall financial conditions were supportive. These Beige Book signals align with SLOOS evidence of easing in key consumer and residential mortgage categories and somewhat looser C&I terms for higher‑quality borrowers, improving the flow of credit. Offsetting factors include persistent supply constraints, elevated input costs, and cautious underwriting in CRE and for lower‑rated firms. Net effect: broader activity gains and firmer credit availability outweigh the headwinds, so the tone shifts slightly more positive, but remains guarded.
